npcs.name: Perrin Hearthvale
npcs.description:
Perrin Hearthvale is a weary but steadfast Centaur marshal who still believes settlements survive only when ordinary people answer one another’s calls for help. As an Asethyr-shaped Centaur, he values freedom, herd-unity, open roads, and honorable defense, but the losses he has survived have left him terrified of formal leadership even while he keeps becoming the person others follow.
In Thornbreak, one of Kharvathen’s mountain towns, Perrin works from the Freeblade Notice Hall coordinating rescue calls, militia watches, refugee escorts, and settlement defense requests. He is humble, guilt-ridden, quietly brave, and fiercely opposed to raider logic, corrupt mercenary contracts, and any “practical” plan that sacrifices civilians for convenience.
npcs.settlementAndAncestryTexture: Thornbreak is a Town in Kharvathen, under Oligarchy, with elevated danger, Farming, Partial forest, Grassland terrain. Local records favor Altruistic, Lawful, Cooperative, Honorable civic habits; common communities include Human, Halfling — Lightfoot Halfling, Halfling — Stout Halfling, Kender, Kithkin. Centaur reads through the Centaur entry of the race compendium, within Animalfolk and Mammalian Anthropomorphs, marked by Iskareth. Half-human, half-equine nomadic hunters who value freedom of movement and open land. Their societies emphasize oral tradition, honor, and herd unity. Table cues: Fey, Charge, Equine Build, Hooves; starting tendency Neutral - Chaotic - Cooperative - Honorable.
rumors: Perrin Hearthvale knows why an ichor ledger changed hands last Anubaday.
Perrin Hearthvale has a contact in Sylvéraith who will deny everything.
plotHooks: Perrin Hearthvale asks the party to protect a household member without revealing why.
A rival faction offers proof that Perrin Hearthvale's public story is incomplete.

npcs.name: Quartermaster Teagren
npcs.description:
Quartermaster Teagren is a practical, smooth-talking Gandirosha supply proctor who knows starvation kills soldiers just as surely as monsters, bad orders, or unstable relics. His luck-touched people are shaped by Thalunesh and Asethyr through charm, timing, revelry, wanderer instincts, and subtle survival magic, which makes him excellent at finding spare ammunition, hidden stores, discounted armor, and the one caravan driver willing to make a dangerous run for the right price.
At the Thornbreak Tavern, Teagren manages Crucible Custodian arms, armor, food stores, thundercoil parts, siege supplies, and questionable “off-ledger” procurement deals that keep patrols alive when official channels fail. He is friendly, mercenary, and morally flexible about sourcing crops, fuel, and diluted ichor medicine, but he is not careless: pure black-market ichor, wasteful commanders, and preventable hunger all offend him because every shortage eventually becomes a body count.
npcs.settlementAndAncestryTexture: Thornbreak is a Town in Kharvathen, under Oligarchy, with elevated danger, Farming, Partial forest, Grassland terrain. Local records favor Altruistic, Lawful, Cooperative, Honorable civic habits; common communities include Human, Halfling — Lightfoot Halfling, Halfling — Stout Halfling, Kender, Kithkin. Gandirosha reads through the Fey-Folk entry of the race compendium, within Fey and Trickster Folk, marked by Thalunesh. Fey-Folk are peoples shaped by glamour, luck, tiny or otherworldly bodies, dreamlike emotion, and trickster magic. At my table, Faerie, Fairy, and Gandirosha are not separate top-level races here; they are bloodlines.
